`nn.GRUCell` implements the same PyTorch GRU equations as `nn.GRU`, but requires explicit timestep/layer loops. Map each layer’s `weight_ih_l{k}`, `weight_hh_l{k}`, `bias_ih_l{k}`, and `bias_hh_l{k}` to its cell, preserving gate order `(reset, update, new)` and both biases. PyTorch applies the reset gate after the candidate recurrent affine transform, including its bias. Multilayer dropout belongs between layers, excluding the final layer; cell loops do not supply it automatically. Matching seeds alone does not guarantee identical dropout masks across implementations. [GRU documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html), [GRUCell documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.modules.rnn.GRUCell.html).

Correctness implication: zero padding embeddings do not prevent recurrent bias updates. Freezing every layer’s hidden state on padded timesteps changes an ordinary unmasked GRU baseline; preserve the supplied baseline’s actual padding behavior when testing equivalence. With the added retention gate fixed exactly to its identity value of one, disable dropout, copy parameters and initial states, then compare all timestep outputs, final states, scores, losses and mapped gradients using tolerance-based assertions. Test mixed history lengths and all-padding handling. For left-padded histories, read the final nonpadding position, never `count-1`.

Expect an eager cell loop to incur more dispatch/kernel overhead than optimized sequence GRU execution; measure rather than assume a slowdown factor. `torch.compile` may reduce overhead, but compilation, graph breaks and recompilation can offset gains. Benchmark representative shapes and full forward/backward/optimizer steps after warmup, using synchronized wall timing or `torch.utils.benchmark`. Record compilation separately, memory and validation overhead. Budget estimate: sum category step times × 200 batches × planned epochs, plus measured overhead; compare eager and compiled break-even costs before committing. [Benchmark guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/recipes/recipes/benchmark.html), [torch.compile](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.compile).
